name: Security Readiness Action Pack
value_proposition: Each quarter, rank the owner's own written account inventory with skip reasons, an owner-approved severity ladder, and a closure log — without scanning, connecting, or certifying anything.
persona: Owner of a 3-20 person salon, clinic, agency, or trades shop with no IT person. They share a POS login, still have a former bookkeeper on payroll access, and have never restored a backup.
problem: Access, backup, and account checks are postponed until something goes wrong. The owner cannot tell which gaps matter this quarter, and a generic turn-on-MFA list does not match the accounts they actually use.
workflow: 1. The person fills the inventory worksheet with one row per business account: account, named_owner, still_with_company (yes/no), mfa (on/off), last_restore_test (a date, never, or n/a), shared_login (yes/no), holds_customer_or_money_data (yes/no), plus the as-of date. Optional: paste a user-list export they already downloaded from Google Workspace or Microsoft 365. This is an owner-typed inventory, not a scan. PERSON DECIDES: which accounts to include, how to spell former-staff names, and whether to paste an optional user list.

2. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to upload the worksheet, paste the rows as text, or not use AI for this data at all.

3. The person pastes the Quarterly Readiness Queue Prompt and their rules from the Skip Rules and Severity Ladder Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the inventory and, if they have one, last quarter's closure log.

4. AI applies skip rules before anything else. It sets aside personal-only accounts (holds_customer_or_money_data = no), accounts the owner marked out of scope, and rows missing an account name. Every skipped row is listed with its reason. Rows missing still_with_company, mfa, or holds_customer_or_money_data are listed under NEEDS YOUR CHECK and are not ranked.

5. AI applies the owner-approved severity ladder to the remaining rows. Default HIGH: former staff still listed; MFA off on an account that holds customer or money data; backup restore never tested on such an account. Default MEDIUM: shared login on an admin account. Rank HIGH then MEDIUM. Never labels the business secure, compliant, or certified.

6. AI labels CONFIRMED fields taken from the inventory, states any AI INTERPRETATION separately, and lists suggested actions. Suggested actions never include scanning, exploiting, connecting to a vendor, changing a password, or disabling an account. PERSON DECIDES: which items, up to 5 this quarter, to act on, who will do each one, and the check date.

7. The person uses the Action Review Checklist before changing anything in a real product. PERSON DECIDES: whether to turn on MFA, remove access, test a restore, or replace a shared login, and they do that work in the real product themselves. The kit changes nothing.

8. The person records each outcome in the quarterly closure log. Closed items stay in the log. Next quarter they re-run on an updated inventory with the Quarter-to-Quarter Update Prompt so HIGH items that closed stay visible if they reopen, and HIGH items still open stay ranked.
before: The owner keeps a mental list (shared iPad, old payroll login, backups they hope exist) and never ranks or re-checks it.
after: Each quarter the owner reviews a ranked action list tied to their own inventory, with skip and severity reasons visible, and a closure log from last quarter. They decide every change in the actual product.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/security-readiness-action-pack using a fictional four-row account inventory dated as of 2026-04-06, with no live systems attached. It shows skip rules setting aside the personal streaming account, a ranked queue of three HIGH items with CONFIRMED fields from the inventory, a fact check of the Payroll row, a mock next-quarter run as of 2026-07-06 where Payroll is closed and the bank portal MFA is still off, and an ending that states the person changes accounts in the real product. The output does not certify the company as secure. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The inventory: show the fictional four-row inventory as a table (Business bank portal, POS admin, Payroll, Owner personal streaming) with the as-of date 2026-04-06 and the default severity ladder (HIGH: former staff still listed; HIGH: MFA off on customer-or-money data; HIGH: restore test = never on customer-or-money data; MEDIUM: shared login on an admin account). Label the table invented. State that no live system is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Skip rules first: list the three skip rules (personal-only; owner-marked out of scope; missing account name), then show exactly 1 skipped account: Owner personal streaming with reason text containing 'personal-only' and 'holds customer or money data = no'.

Step 3 of 6 - The ranked queue: show 3 HIGH items in order (Payroll, Business bank portal, POS admin), each with a CONFIRMED line from the inventory and a severity reason. Show the sentence 'This does not certify the company as secure.' Show AI INTERPRETATION: none of these rows prove an account was misused; they only repeat what you entered. Show RECOMMENDED ACTION: pick up to 5 items, assign who will do them, and set a check date.

Step 4 of 6 - Check the facts: open the Payroll row. A 'Check facts against the inventory row' button shows three rows (still_with_company no vs no, named_owner J. Reed vs J. Reed, holds_customer_or_money_data yes vs yes), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - Closure log and next quarter: show the fictional closure log after the quarter of 2026-04-06, then a mock run as of 2026-07-06. Payroll is listed as closed with text containing 'access removed on 2026-04-18'. Business bank portal is still HIGH with text containing 'MFA still off'. POS admin is still HIGH with text containing 'MFA still off'. Owner personal streaming stays skipped as personal-only.

Step 6 of 6 - You change it: state the exact sentences 'You change it in the real product. The kit changes nothing.' and 'This does not certify the company as secure.' Explain that the person turns on MFA, removes access, tests a restore, or replaces a shared login in the real product, and that nothing is scanned, disabled, or changed automatically. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All accounts, names, and dates on this page are fictional. No real business data is used, and nothing is connected to a bank, POS, payroll, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or any other live system.

kit_contents.title: Quarterly Security Readiness Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for the quarterly run. It covers filling the inventory columns (account, named_owner, still_with_company, mfa, last_restore_test, shared_login, holds_customer_or_money_data) and the as-of date, the optional pasted user-list export from Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading, and the rule that this is an owner inventory, not a scan. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Quarterly Readiness Queue Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that applies skip rules first, applies the owner-approved severity ladder, ranks HIGH then MEDIUM, lists every skip with its reason, and labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It forbids scanning, connecting, changing passwords, disabling accounts, inventing MFA or backup status, and labelling the business secure, compliant, or certified.

kit_contents.title: Quarter-to-Quarter Update Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt for the following quarter. It reads the previous closure log with the new inventory, keeps closed HIGH items in the log so they are not forgotten if they reopen, ranks HIGH items that are still open, and forbids scanning, connecting, or certifying the company as secure.

kit_contents.title: Skip Rules and Severity Ladder Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person lists accounts to mark out of scope and confirms or turns off each default HIGH and MEDIUM rule. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the queue prompt. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Quarterly Closure Log Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (quarter_of, account, named_owner, action_taken, outcome, check_date, notes) with the allowed outcome values (closed, still open, skipped, deferred) and fictional example rows. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Action Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before changing anything in a real product. It confirms that CONFIRMED fields match the inventory row, that skip reasons are listed, that the output does not certify the company as secure, that at most 5 actions were picked with a person and a check date, and that the person will make any change in the real product themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Inventory
kit_contents.purpose: The same four-row fictional CSV used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real account names.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling access and former-staff names in AI tools: review data settings, keep former-staff names only as the owner typed them and delete them from the AI chat after the run, do not paste passwords or MFA secrets, do not scan or test systems the owner does not own, and do not disable the only POS login until a named login works. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is scanned, disabled, or changed automatically.

decision_rules: Use the inventory's as-of date, not today's date. If the inventory has no as-of date, ask the person for it before building the queue.
Apply all skip rules before ranking. Skipped accounts are never ranked and never given a HIGH or MEDIUM label.
Skip any row whose holds_customer_or_money_data value is no. Show the reason 'personal-only; holds customer or money data = no'.
Skip any account the owner marked out of scope. Show the reason 'marked out of scope by you'.
Skip any row missing an account name. Show the reason 'missing an account name'.
If a remaining row is missing still_with_company, mfa, or holds_customer_or_money_data, or the same account name appears twice, do not rank it. List it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Do not invent MFA status, restore-test dates, employment status, or shared-login flags. Use only values the person entered. last_restore_test = n/a is not treated as never.

Default HIGH, in this rank order within HIGH: still_with_company = no (former staff still listed); then mfa = off and holds_customer_or_money_data = yes; then last_restore_test = never and holds_customer_or_money_data = yes. An account that matches more than one HIGH rule stays one row and lists every matching reason.
Default MEDIUM: shared_login = yes on an admin account. If the same account is already HIGH, list MEDIUM as an extra reason on that HIGH row; do not create a second row.
Rank every HIGH row before any MEDIUM-only row. Never output a LOW band in this version.
Never use the words secure, compliant, certified, audit passed, or hardened as a claim about the business. Every queue must include the sentence 'This does not certify the company as secure.'

Suggested actions may only tell the person what to do themselves in the real product: remove access, turn on MFA, run a restore test and record the date, or give a shared admin login a named owner. Do not suggest a scan, a penetration test, an exploit, an OAuth connection, a password change performed by the kit, or disabling an account from the kit.
If a shared POS or admin login is flagged, the suggested action must warn the person not to turn off the shared login until a named login can open that product.
Recommend at most 5 actions this quarter. If more HIGH items remain, list them as 'not in this quarter's five; keep in the log'.
AI INTERPRETATION must state that the rows only repeat what the owner entered and do not prove that an account was misused.

On a later quarter, match closure-log entries to the new inventory by account name. Closed items stay in the log. If a closed account is still listed in the new inventory with the same HIGH reason, return it to the HIGH queue as still open. If it is gone from the inventory, list it under CLOSED and keep the log row.
human_ai_boundary: AI applies skip rules and lists every skipped account with its reason. The person decides which accounts are personal-only or out of scope, and whether to override a skip.
AI applies the severity ladder the owner approved. The person sets the ladder and decides whether a HIGH or MEDIUM label is fair.
AI ranks the queue from the written inventory. The person decides which items, up to 5 this quarter, to act on, who will do them, and the check date.
AI suggests actions using only inventory fields. The person checks every CONFIRMED field against the inventory row before doing anything in a real product.
AI never connects to a vendor, scans a system, changes a password, disables an account, or turns on MFA. The person makes every change in the real product, or decides not to.
AI reads the closure log. Only the person records outcomes, and the log reflects what the person entered, not what AI assumed.
AI labels CONFIRMED facts (from the inventory or log), AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, scanned, disabled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person changes accounts in the real product and that the kit changes nothing.

Atlas does not connect to a bank, POS, payroll, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, no network scan, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading an inventory to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to keep former-staff names only as they typed them.
The kit tells the person to delete former-staff names from the AI chat after the run, and not to paste passwords, recovery codes, or MFA secrets.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.
The kit tells the person not to scan, probe, or test systems they do not own, and not to treat the output as a reason to do so.
Shared-login flags must not tell the person to lock out the only person who can open the POS. The suggested action is to add a named owner first.
The queue never labels the business secure, compliant, or certified. Incomplete inventories can miss HIGH items; the page says the ranking only reflects rows the owner entered.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout.
required_data_tools: Owner inventory worksheet (template in the kit)
Optional user-list export from Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 (CSV), names of people no longer employed kept only as the owner typed them
Quarterly closure log (template in the kit)
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings.

The guided demo is a six-step stepper. It shows the text 'Step N of 6', a 'Next step' button (absent or disabled on step 6), and a 'Previous step' button (absent or disabled on step 1). Each step has a visible heading.

Step 1 shows a table with exactly 4 data rows whose account names are Business bank portal, POS admin, Payroll, and Owner personal streaming. It also shows the as-of date 2026-04-06 and the severity ladder text 'former staff still listed', 'MFA off on customer-or-money data', 'restore test = never on customer-or-money data', and 'shared login on an admin account'.
Step 2 lists exactly 1 skipped account: Owner personal streaming with reason text containing 'personal-only' and 'holds customer or money data = no'.

Step 3 lists exactly 3 queued accounts in this order: Payroll, Business bank portal, POS admin. Payroll is HIGH with text containing 'former staff still listed'. Business bank portal is HIGH with text containing 'MFA' and 'never'. POS admin is HIGH with text containing 'MFA off' and MEDIUM with text containing 'shared'.

Step 3 shows the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone. It also shows the exact sentence 'This does not certify the company as secure.' The AI INTERPRETATION line states that the rows only repeat what you entered and do not prove an account was misused.

Step 4 shows the Payroll CONFIRMED line with still_with_company = no. Activating 'Check facts against the inventory row' reveals three rows (still_with_company, named_owner, holds_customer_or_money_data), each containing the text 'Matches', and the values no, J. Reed, and yes.

Step 5 shows the fictional closure log and a mock next-quarter run as of 2026-07-06. The run lists Payroll as closed with text containing 'access removed on 2026-04-18', lists Business bank portal as still HIGH with text containing 'MFA still off', lists POS admin as still HIGH with text containing 'MFA still off', and lists Owner personal streaming as skipped with text containing 'personal-only'.
